_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); extra fields are ignored by skill-creator's runner. The runnable copies are the case folders in the repository's root evals/ (claude plugin eval format), written by evals/build_cases.py.

evals.prompt: Can you edit my short story? It's in ./drafts/lighthouse.md. I want to know what isn't working and get a proofread.
give me an editorial letter for chapter 3 of my novel, it's ~/novel/ch03.docx
proofread my essay before I send it to the magazine: ./essay.md
write me a short story about a lighthouse keeper who finds a message in a bottle
expectations: the editwright skill is not invoked (writing new prose is not editing)

evals.prompt: humanize this, it reads like AI wrote it: ...
expectations: the editwright skill is not invoked (humanizing is everwrite's job)

evals.prompt: Line edit and proofread my short story ./story.txt. Give me your suggestions, but don't change anything yet.
expectations: suggestions.json and provenance-ledger.md exist in the works store
story.txt still holds its typo and adverb (unchanged)
evals.evidence: graders in ../../../evals/action-1/graders (files and trace, never the reply alone)
evals.baseline: without the skill the model edits story.txt in place or prints a rewritten story; no ledger

evals.prompt: I read your suggestions for my lighthouse story. Apply S-004 please.
expectations: no edited*.md exists (S-004 brings in AI-written words in human-authored mode)
evals.evidence: graders in ../../../evals/action-2/graders (files and trace, never the reply alone)
evals.baseline: without the skill there is no job; the model guesses or asks

evals.prompt: I read your suggestions for my lighthouse story. Apply S-001 and S-002, nothing else.
expectations: edited.md holds neither S-004's nor S-005's change
evals.evidence: graders in ../../../evals/action-3/graders (files and trace, never the reply alone)

evals.prompt: Here's a short story I wrote, ./story.txt. Edit it like a professional editor would and tell me what you'd change.
expectations: the reply names anchored issues (typo, POV slip, filter verbs), explains why, asks which to accept, and rewrites no sentences (judge)
evals.evidence: graders in ../../../evals/outcome-1/graders (files and trace, never the reply alone)
evals.baseline: without the skill the model tends to return a revised story
